title: Learning-based Optimization of the Under-sampling Pattern in MRI (LOUPE); journal version: "Deep-learning-based Optimization of the Under-sampling Pattern in MRI"
authors: Conference (IPMI) version: Cagla Deniz Bahadir, Adrian V. Dalca, Mert R. Sabuncu. Journal (IEEE TCI) version: Cagla D. Bahadir, Alan Q. Wang, Adrian V. Dalca, Mert R. Sabuncu.
venue: IPMI 2019 (Information Processing in Medical Imaging), Springer LNCS 11492, pp. 780-792. Extended journal version: IEEE Transactions on Computational Imaging, vol. 6, pp. 1139-1152, 2020.
method_summary: LOUPE is an end-to-end supervised deep-learning framework that jointly optimizes (1) WHERE to sample in k-space and (2) HOW to reconstruct, for accelerated (compressed-sensing) MRI. Step by step: it parameterizes the 2D Cartesian k-space sampling mask as a set of learnable per-frequency (Bernoulli) sampling probabilities; during training it applies a differentiable relaxation (sigmoid probabilities + a rescaling to hit a target sparsity, plus a straight-through / Gumbel-style stochastic sampling of the binary mask) so gradients can flow to the mask parameters. Full-resolution training scans are retrospectively under-sampled with the current mask, and the masked measurements are fed to a U-Net anti-aliasing/reconstruction network; the reconstruction is compared to the fully-sampled ground truth, and both the mask probabilities and the U-Net weights are trained together by minimizing reconstruction loss under a sparsity constraint. The output is a single OFFLINE-optimized probabilistic sampling distribution (a fixed mask realized per acceleration factor / per anatomy) plus a trained reconstruction network. At inference the mask is fixed and non-adaptive: it does not change per-scan and does not use any per-instance uncertainty. It is MRI-k-space specific and demonstrated on brain and knee datasets, showing the learned masks are data/anatomy-dependent and outperform random/variable-density/equispaced patterns.
uses_ensemble_or_policy: It requires OFFLINE mask optimization (training) — this is its core mechanism. It also trains a reconstruction network (U-Net) jointly. It does NOT use a diffusion prior, does NOT use posterior sampling, and does NOT require an ensemble of posterior samples at inference (no NFE concept — reconstruction is a single feed-forward U-Net pass). It is not a reinforcement-learning "policy network" in the sequential-decision sense, but it is a fully trained/optimized system: the learnable sampling probabilities are optimized end-to-end via SGD on a dataset, and the resulting mask is fixed/static at test time (non-adaptive, not per-instance, not mid-acquisition).
overlap_with_ours: Overlap is only at the high-level GOAL — both PVAS and LOUPE decide which k-space measurements to acquire to improve reconstruction. Beyond that the mechanisms are disjoint. LOUPE does NOT cover any of PVAS's distinctive components: (a) single-trajectory Tweedie-second-moment / Jacobian posterior-variance estimation — LOUPE has no diffusion model, no Tweedie, no denoiser-Jacobian, no variance estimate at all; (b) variance-gated Kalman-style data-consistency update — absent (LOUPE reconstruction is a trained U-Net, not a per-frequency gain from posterior variance vs noise); (c) mid-trajectory / per-instance ACTIVE acquisition — LOUPE's mask is optimized offline and is FIXED at test time (same mask for all scans at a given acceleration/anatomy); it is population-level sampling design, not instance-adaptive online acquisition; (d) multi-domain generality — LOUPE is specific to MRI 2D Cartesian k-space and requires retraining per setting. Crucially, PVAS is TRAINING-FREE and needs no retraining or reconstruction network, whereas LOUPE's entire value proposition is the joint offline training of mask + reconstructor. So LOUPE covers none of PVAS's core claims; it is the archetypal "trained, offline, non-adaptive" contrast case that PVAS positions itself against.

title: Denoising Diffusion Restoration Models
authors: Bahjat Kawar, Michael Elad, Stefano Ermon, Jiaming Song
venue: NeurIPS 2022 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35, Main Conference Track)
method_summary: DDRM is a training-free posterior sampler for noisy linear inverse problems y = Hx + z that reuses a pretrained unconditional diffusion model. It computes the SVD H = U*Sigma*V^T and defines the entire variational diffusion process in the spectral space x_bar_t = V^T x_t, treating each spectral coordinate separately by its singular value s_i: null-space coordinates (s_i = 0) are synthesized by ordinary unconditional diffusion, while measured coordinates are updated by analytically mixing the transformed measurement y_bar_i with the denoiser's x0-prediction. The mixing gain is a closed-form function of the schedule noise sigma_t, the measurement noise sigma_y, and s_i — e.g., when sigma_t >= sigma_y/s_i it uses eta_b-weighted Wiener-like interpolation, and otherwise nudges x0_hat toward y_bar with weight sqrt(1-eta^2)*sigma_t/(sigma_y/s_i) — so data consistency is variance-aware by construction rather than by estimation. A theorem shows a pretrained DDPM/DDIM optimum is also optimal for the DDRM objective, so no task-specific training is needed. At inference it runs a single sampling trajectory with only 20 NFEs (20 uniformly spaced steps of a 1000-step pretrained model, eta=0.85, eta_b=1), and was demonstrated on super-resolution, deblurring, inpainting, and colorization on ImageNet and other datasets, 5x faster than the nearest unsupervised competitor.
uses_ensemble_or_policy: None of the three. No policy network and no offline/task-specific training (it provably reuses the unconditional DDPM/DDIM prior; only H and its SVD change per task). At inference it is a single trajectory of ~20 NFEs producing one posterior sample per image; the quantitative tables report single samples (the paper shows multiple samples only to illustrate diversity, Fig. 5), so no ensemble of posterior samples is required.
overlap_with_ours: Overlaps with part of our contribution (a): DDRM already performs per-frequency, noise-aware, Wiener/Kalman-flavored data consistency in the operator's spectral domain — its per-coordinate gains depend on sigma_t, sigma_y, and singular value s_i, which is conceptually close to our gain P_i/(P_i + sigma_noise^2). Critical difference: DDRM's per-coordinate 'variances' are fixed analytically by the noise schedule via its variational construction (q(x_t|x_0) = N(x_0, sigma_t^2 I)); it does NOT estimate the actual posterior variance diag Cov[x0|xt] from the denoiser Jacobian / Tweedie's second-moment identity, uses no Hutchinson probes or JVPs, and its gain is image-content-independent (same for every image at a given t), whereas our P_i is instance-adaptive. It does NOT cover: (b) active/adaptive measurement selection — measurements are assumed given and fixed, with no mid-trajectory acquisition; single-trajectory Tweedie-Jacobian variance estimation; variance maps for uncertainty-driven acquisition scoring; and it requires an accessible SVD of H, limiting operator generality relative to our DPS/PiGDM-style guidance. Also no MRI/CT experiments (only SR, deblurring, inpainting, colorization).

title: Diffusion Posterior Sampling for General Noisy Inverse Problems
authors: Hyungjin Chung, Jeongsol Kim, Michael T. McCann, Marc L. Klasky, Jong Chul Ye
venue: ICLR 2023 (The Eleventh International Conference on Learning Representations), spotlight / notable-top-25%
method_summary: DPS is a training-free posterior sampler for noisy (non)linear inverse problems using a pretrained unconditional diffusion prior. At each ancestral (DDPM) sampling step it evaluates the score network, forms the posterior-mean estimate x0_hat = E[x0|xt] via Tweedie's (first-moment) formula, and approximates the intractable time-dependent likelihood p(y|xt) by p(y|x0_hat) (a Laplace/Jensen-gap-bounded approximation). It then adds a guidance gradient -zeta * grad_xt ||y - A(x0_hat)||^2 (weighted-norm variant for Poisson noise) to the standard denoising update, with a scalar step size zeta_i = zeta'/||y - A(x0_hat)|| — i.e., soft gradient guidance rather than hard measurement-consistency projection. Computing the guidance requires backpropagating through the denoiser (a VJP), so each step costs roughly one forward score evaluation plus one backward pass; a single trajectory yields a single reconstruction. It is demonstrated on inpainting, 4x super-resolution, Gaussian/motion deblurring, Fourier phase retrieval, and nonlinear deblurring, all with measurement operators fixed a priori. Verified from the arXiv abs page, ar5iv full text, and the ICLR 2023 poster page.
uses_ensemble_or_policy: No policy network, no offline mask optimization, no ensemble. Inference is a single sampling trajectory producing one posterior sample; per step it uses one score-network forward pass plus one backprop through the score network for the likelihood gradient (~2 NFE-equivalents per step, standard DDPM step counts, e.g. 1000). The measurement operator/mask is fixed before sampling and never adapted.
overlap_with_ours: Covers: the base solver framework PVAS sits on top of — training-free guidance with a pretrained unconditional diffusion prior, Tweedie FIRST-moment estimate x0_hat = E[x0|xt], gradient-based soft data consistency, single trajectory, generality across linear/nonlinear noisy operators. Does NOT cover: (a) any posterior VARIANCE/covariance estimation — no second-order Tweedie identity, no denoiser-Jacobian diagonal, no Hutchinson/JVP probes, no uncertainty maps; (b) variance-gated Kalman-style data consistency — DPS uses a single scalar step size zeta for all measurement coordinates, not per-frequency gains P_i/(P_i+sigma^2); (c) active/adaptive measurement selection — the mask/operator is fixed a priori, nothing is acquired mid-trajectory; (d) matched-budget active-sensing evaluation. DPS is the baseline/backbone PVAS extends, not a competitor to its contributions.

title: Active MR k-space Sampling with Reinforcement Learning
authors: Luis Pineda, Sumana Basu, Adriana Romero, Roberto Calandra, Michal Drozdzal
venue: MICCAI 2020 (Medical Image Computing and Computer Assisted Intervention, Springer LNCS vol. 12262, pp. 23-33)
method_summary: The paper formulates active MRI acquisition as a POMDP: the hidden state is (ground-truth image, current sampling mask), the observation is (current reconstruction, mask), actions are unobserved k-space column indices, and the reward is the decrease in reconstruction error after acquiring the chosen line, R = C(x_hat_{t+1}, x) - C(x_hat_t, x). A Double DQN (DDQN) value network is trained offline with this reward on top of a FIXED pretrained CNN reconstruction model (the evaluator/reconstructor architecture of Zhang et al., their ref [31]); reconstructor and policy are trained in stages, not jointly. Two variants are proposed: ss-ddqn (subject-specific, Q-network conditions on the current reconstruction and mask, giving per-subject adaptive trajectories) and ds-ddqn (dataset-specific, conditions only on the time step, yielding one fixed trajectory for all subjects — effectively offline mask/trajectory optimization; it slightly outperforms ss-ddqn in their experiments). At deployment, the next k-space line is chosen greedily as argmax of the learned Q-values over valid actions. Experiments use single-coil knee data from fastMRI (approx. 19.9k train / 1.8k val / 1.85k test slices), reporting MSE/NMSE/PSNR/SSIM AUC across acceleration factors against Random, Random-LB, LowToHigh, Evaluator, and one-step Oracle baselines, with DDQN outperforming all heuristics. The reconstruction is a deterministic single forward pass per step; there is no posterior variance, uncertainty estimation, ensembling, or diffusion model anywhere in the method.
uses_ensemble_or_policy: Yes — it requires a trained policy: a DDQN value network trained offline via RL (with epsilon-greedy exploration and reward computed against ground-truth images), on top of a separately pretrained, fixed CNN reconstruction network. The ds-ddqn variant amounts to offline trajectory/mask optimization (one trajectory reused for all subjects). It uses NO ensemble of posterior samples and no diffusion model: inference costs one deterministic reconstruction-network forward pass plus one Q-network forward pass per acquisition step (no sampling, no NFE budget in the diffusion sense).
overlap_with_ours: Covers: the overall task framing of PVAS component (b) — sequential, mid-acquisition active selection of MRI k-space lines given a fixed reconstruction model, evaluated on fastMRI knee across many acceleration factors (it is the canonical RL baseline for exactly this task, with public code at facebookresearch/active-mri-acquisition). Its subject-specific variant also adapts the trajectory to the current reconstruction, like our mid-trajectory selection. Does NOT cover: (i) any uncertainty/posterior-variance-based acquisition scoring — lines are picked by a learned Q-function, not by projected posterior variance; (ii) diffusion priors or posterior sampling of any kind; (iii) single-trajectory Tweedie-Jacobian (Hutchinson-probe JVP) variance estimation — no posterior moments are computed at all; (iv) our variance-gated Kalman-style data-consistency update, component (a) — their reconstruction is a fixed feed-forward CNN with no data-consistency gain; (v) training-free operation — it needs RL training of a policy network plus a trained reconstructor, whereas PVAS needs neither; (vi) multi-domain generality — MRI single-coil knee only, no CT angles or compressive imaging; notably their finding that a non-adaptive dataset-level trajectory (ds-ddqn) matched the adaptive policy is a result we should discuss when arguing for per-subject adaptivity.

title: Experimental design for MRI by greedy policy search
authors: Tim Bakker, Herke van Hoof, Max Welling
venue: NeurIPS 2020 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33), spotlight
method_summary: The paper frames sequential k-space column selection for accelerated MRI as a POMDP and learns an adaptive acquisition policy with policy gradient methods (REINFORCE with parallel trajectory baselines, q=8 rollouts during training). A CNN policy network (~4.7M parameters) takes the current U-Net reconstruction as input and outputs a softmax distribution over unacquired k-space columns; the reward is the per-step improvement in SSIM of the reconstruction. The reconstructor is a fixed, pretrained fastMRI U-Net (deterministic, not generative) that maps zero-filled reconstructions to images; the policy and reconstructor are not jointly trained. The central finding is that a greedy one-step-ahead policy objective performs nearly on par with the non-greedy full-horizon objective, which the authors attribute to higher gradient-estimate variance hampering the non-greedy model's per-image adaptivity. At test time, acquisition alternates: reconstruct, feed the image to the policy net, pick a column, re-reconstruct, until the budget is reached (e.g., 8x->4x and 32x->4x acceleration on fastMRI single-coil knee 128x128 and brain 256x256). Baselines include non-adaptive heuristics, a dataset-level oracle mask, and an AlphaZero-style MCTS approach, which the greedy policy outperforms at much lower cost. No diffusion models, posterior sampling, posterior variance, information-gain criteria, or uncertainty quantification of any kind are used.
uses_ensemble_or_policy: Yes - it fundamentally requires a TRAINED POLICY NETWORK: a ~4.7M-parameter CNN trained offline with policy gradients (REINFORCE) on fastMRI data, per anatomy/setting, plus a pretrained U-Net reconstructor. No ensemble of posterior samples is used at inference (the reconstructor is deterministic; one policy forward + one U-Net forward per acquired line, so roughly 2 network evaluations per acquisition step along a single trajectory). Training, however, uses q=8 parallel rollouts for gradient-variance reduction. There is no offline mask optimization in the learned-fixed-mask sense (masks are adaptive per image), but the policy itself is entirely offline-trained.
overlap_with_ours: Covers: (a) per-image ADAPTIVE/active sequential selection of MRI k-space lines under a measurement budget - the same task as PVAS's active-selection component in the MRI domain; (b) sequential closed-loop acquisition interleaved with reconstruction; (c) evidence that per-image adaptivity beats fixed/heuristic masks, with budget-matched comparisons; (d) greedy one-step-ahead selection as a strong strategy (conceptually adjacent to our greedy variance-scoring rule). Does NOT cover: training-free operation (it needs an offline-trained policy network per dataset/setting - the exact dependency PVAS eliminates); diffusion priors or posterior sampling of any kind; single-trajectory Tweedie second-moment / denoiser-Jacobian posterior-variance estimation (no uncertainty estimation at all - selection is learned, not variance-scored); variance-gated Kalman-style data consistency (its U-Net has no probabilistic data-consistency mechanism); MID-DIFFUSION-TRAJECTORY acquisition (its loop is over measurements with a feed-forward reconstructor, not over diffusion timesteps); multi-domain generality (MRI-only; no CT angles, inpainting, or compressive sensing); matched-NFE evaluation against diffusion solvers. Reconstruction quality is also bounded by a small deterministic U-Net rather than a generative prior.

title: End-to-End Sequential Sampling and Reconstruction for MRI
authors: Tianwei Yin, Zihui Wu, He Sun, Adrian V. Dalca, Yisong Yue, Katherine L. Bouman
venue: Proceedings of Machine Learning for Health (ML4H), PMLR volume 158, pages 261-281
method_summary: Note the exact title is "...for MRI", not "...for Accelerated MRI" (an early preprint variant was titled "...for MR Imaging"). The paper proposes a fully differentiable co-design framework that jointly trains (1) a sequential sampling policy and (2) a reconstructor for accelerated MRI. At each acquisition step, a trained sampler network (a 5-layer MLP for 1D k-space line selection, or an 8-block UNet for 2D point selection) takes the past k-space measurements, the current k-space reconstruction, and the current sampling mask, and outputs a probability heatmap over candidate k-space samples; the next measurement is drawn stochastically from this distribution, so the acquisition adapts per-subject in closed loop. The reconstructor is a standard 8-block U-Net mapping the zero-filled complex image to a real-valued image, applied after each acquisition step. The whole pipeline is trained end-to-end with supervised (SSIM-based) losses, using a straight-through estimator (binary mask indicator in the forward pass, sigmoid relaxation for gradients) to backpropagate through the discrete sampling decisions. At inference, each acquisition step requires one forward pass through sampler and reconstructor; there is no ensemble, no posterior sampling, and no uncertainty/variance estimation. It uses no diffusion or score-based generative prior anywhere. Baselines include LOUPE (learned fixed masks), PG-MRI (RL policy), an uncertainty-driven greedy "Evaluator" policy, and random/equispaced/spectrum heuristics; on fastMRI knee it outperforms LOUPE on over 96% of test samples. Demonstrated only on MRI.
uses_ensemble_or_policy: Yes - it requires a trained policy network (sampler MLP/UNet) co-trained end-to-end with a trained U-Net reconstructor via supervised learning on fastMRI, i.e., offline training of both components is mandatory. The sampling is adaptive at test time (not an offline-fixed mask), but only through the learned policy. It does NOT use an ensemble of posterior samples, Bayesian posterior sampling, or any generative/diffusion prior; inference is one deterministic sampler+reconstructor forward pass per acquisition step (no notion of NFEs in the diffusion sense).
overlap_with_ours: Covers: the high-level idea of subject-adaptive, mid-acquisition ("sequential") selection of k-space measurements using intermediate reconstruction information - so PVAS cannot claim adaptive/sequential MRI sampling per se as novel, and this is a canonical learned-policy baseline we should compare against or discuss. Does NOT cover: anything training-free (it needs joint offline training of policy + reconstructor and is tied to the training distribution/operator); diffusion priors or posterior sampling of any kind; posterior-variance estimation (no uncertainty quantification at all - its acquisition scores come from a learned heatmap, not from Cov[x0|xt]); our single-trajectory Tweedie-Jacobian variance estimate with a Hutchinson finite-difference JVP; variance-gated Kalman-style data-consistency updates; mid-diffusion-trajectory acquisition interleaved with sampling steps; matched-NFE evaluation; and multi-domain generality (MRI only - no CT angles, inpainting, or compressive sensing). Every technical mechanism in PVAS is disjoint; the overlap is at the problem-formulation level (active sequential k-space sampling) only.

title: Improving Diffusion Models for Inverse Problems Using Optimal Posterior Covariance
authors: Xinyu Peng, Ziyang Zheng, Wenrui Dai, Nuoqian Xiao, Chenglin Li, Junni Zou, Hongkai Xiong
venue: ICML 2024 (Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR vol. 235, pp. 40347-40370)
method_summary: Peng et al. show that zero-shot diffusion solvers (DPS, PiGDM, DDNM, DiffPIR) can all be read as replacing the intractable denoising posterior p(x0|xt) with a Gaussian N(D_t(xt), Sigma_t) whose covariance is hand-crafted and isotropic, and they propose replacing it with a 'optimal' covariance obtained by (variational) maximum-likelihood. They give two plug-and-play, training-free routes: (i) 'Convert' — a fixed-point formula (Thm 4.2) that converts the learned reverse-variance output head of pretrained iDDPM-style models into a per-pixel diagonal posterior variance of x0|xt; and (ii) 'Analytic' — offline Monte Carlo estimation of timestep-dependent posterior variances when no variance head exists. They additionally propose a trained option: learning posterior covariance prediction in an orthonormal basis (DCT/DWT), which requires training a separate checkpoint (e.g., ffhq_dwt.ckpt in their repo). The covariance is then used in Type I (DPS/PiGDM-style) guidance via the likelihood N(y | A D_t(xt), sigma^2 I + A Sigma_t A^T) (inverted in closed form for isotropic cases or by conjugate gradient in general), and in Type II (DiffPIR/DDNM-style) guidance as a Mahalanobis-weighted proximal/data-consistency step — which for diagonalizable operators is exactly a per-coordinate Wiener/Kalman-type gain. Experiments cover inpainting, deblurring, and super-resolution on natural-image datasets (FFHQ/ImageNet-type); no MRI or CT experiments, and no discussion of Tweedie's second-moment identity or denoiser-Jacobian variance estimation.
uses_ensemble_or_policy: No policy network and no active acquisition of any kind. Inference is a single sampling trajectory with standard sampler NFEs — no ensemble of posterior samples at inference. However, the variance itself is not estimated from the trajectory: 'Convert' requires a pretrained diffusion model that has a learned reverse-variance head (iDDPM-style training objective); 'Analytic' requires an offline Monte-Carlo precomputation of per-timestep variances before inference; and the strongest variant (DWT/DCT-basis covariance prediction) requires offline training of a new variance-prediction checkpoint. So: no ensemble at test time, no policy, but two of three variance sources depend on the model's trained variance head or offline training/precomputation rather than on-the-fly estimation.
overlap_with_ours: Covers (substantially) our component (a): the core idea of plugging per-coordinate posterior variance diag Cov[x0|xt] into the data-consistency/guidance step is exactly this paper's contribution — their Type I likelihood sigma^2 I + A Sigma A^T and Type II Mahalanobis proximal step reduce, for masked-Fourier/diagonal operators, to precisely the per-frequency Kalman gain P_i/(P_i + sigma_noise^2) we propose. We cannot claim novelty for 'variance-gated data consistency' per se; we can only claim a different variance ESTIMATOR. Does NOT cover: (1) single-trajectory, training-free variance estimation via Tweedie's second-moment identity (sigma_t^2 * denoiser Jacobian) with a Hutchinson probe / finite-difference JVP — they never touch the denoiser Jacobian and their training-free routes need either an iDDPM variance head or offline Monte Carlo (note: the Jacobian-based estimator itself is closer to TMPD, Boys et al., which appears in their comparison tables — check that separately); (2) ACTIVE measurement selection / mid-trajectory adaptive acquisition — completely absent; (3) MRI k-space, CT angles, or any medical/multi-operator evaluation — they only do inpainting/deblurring/super-resolution on natural images; (4) matched-budget acquisition evaluation. Our headline novelty (mid-trajectory active sensing driven by projected posterior variance) is untouched by this paper.

title: Active Diffusion Subsampling
authors: Oisín Nolan, Tristan S. W. Stevens, Wessel L. van Nierop, Ruud J. G. van Sloun (Eindhoven University of Technology)
venue: Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR), accepted 11 Mar 2025; first posted arXiv June 2024 (v2 April 2025)
method_summary: ADS runs a single guided reverse-diffusion trajectory (DPS-style gradient guidance with fixed step size zeta on a pretrained unconditional diffusion prior) while maintaining a batch of Np=16 particles that implicitly track a belief distribution over the clean signal x0. At reverse-diffusion steps on a fixed subsampling schedule S (e.g., every ~50-100 steps), each particle is converted to a clean estimate x_hat_0 via Tweedie's first-moment formula, projected into measurement space (y_hat_i = A x_hat_0), and the predicted measurements are modeled as an isotropic Gaussian mixture across particles; a closed-form GMM entropy approximation scores each candidate measurement location, and the maximum-entropy (maximum particle-disagreement) measurement is acquired next and folded into the DPS guidance term. This requires no policy network, no task-specific retraining, and no offline mask optimization — just a measurement model — and works at any subsampling rate. Uncertainty is computed purely as empirical spread among the 16 particle predictions; the paper never uses denoiser Jacobians, Hutchinson probes, or Tweedie's second-moment covariance identity, and data consistency is plain DPS with a constant scalar guidance weight (no variance-weighted/Kalman gain). Experiments: MNIST pixel/line subsampling, CelebA 4x4-box subsampling, fastMRI k-space line selection at 4x acceleration (competitive with supervised PG-MRI, LOUPE, SeqMRI), and cardiac ultrasound (CAMUS) scan-line selection; no CT angles or generic compressive-sensing matrices. Appendix A.8 reports 8-16 particles suffice with diminishing returns; runtime ~40 ms/step with ~76 steps per acquisition on fastMRI (RTX 2080 Ti).
uses_ensemble_or_policy: ENSEMBLE, yes: it maintains Np=16 posterior-sample particles through one reverse trajectory, so the score network is evaluated Np times per diffusion step (total NFE = 16 x T; e.g., 16 x ~400-600 steps for CelebA, ~76 steps per acquisition on fastMRI). Policy network: NO — measurement selection is an analytic max-entropy rule over the particle GMM. Offline training / mask optimization: NO — training-free with any pretrained diffusion prior, only a measurement model is specified.
overlap_with_ours: ALREADY COVERS: the conceptual core of our part (b) — training-free, policy-network-free ACTIVE measurement selection performed mid-trajectory inside a single reverse-diffusion run of a pretrained prior, scoring candidate measurements by posterior uncertainty projected into measurement space, demonstrated on MRI k-space line selection (plus MNIST pixels, CelebA boxes, ultrasound scan lines — so partial multi-domain generality too). Any claim like 'first training-free diffusion-based active acquisition' is dead. DOES NOT COVER: (i) single-trajectory variance estimation — ADS needs a 16-particle ensemble (16x NFE per step), whereas we estimate diag Cov[x0|xt] from ONE trajectory via Tweedie's second-moment identity with a single Hutchinson finite-difference JVP probe (2 extra denoiser calls/step); ADS never touches denoiser Jacobians or Tweedie covariance; (ii) our part (a) entirely — ADS uses plain fixed-weight DPS guidance with no variance-gated Kalman-style data-consistency gain P_i/(P_i+sigma^2); (iii) variance-map smoothing (e.g., radial in k-space); (iv) matched-budget AND matched-NFE evaluation (ADS's 16x NFE overhead is exactly the axis we can beat it on); (v) CT projection angles and generic compressive-sensing operators.

title: Enhancing Diffusion Models for Inverse Problems with Covariance-Aware Posterior Sampling
venue: arXiv preprint (cs.CV, cs.AI); no conference/journal acceptance found on OpenReview, ADS, or proceedings searches as of July 2026
method_summary: CA-DPS is a training-free modification of DPS-style posterior sampling for noisy linear inverse problems with a pretrained unconditional DDPM. Its Theorem 1 extends Tweedie's formula to second moments, giving the closed form Cov(x0|xt) = ((1-abar_t)/abar_t) * (I + (1-abar_t) * Hessian of log p_t(xt)) — i.e., the posterior covariance depends on the Hessian of the score. In practice they approximate only the DIAGONAL of this Hessian by a finite difference of the score vectors at consecutive timesteps t and t-1 along the same sampling trajectory (H_t ~ [score(x_t,t) - score(x_{t-1},t-1)]/(t-(t-1))), reusing score evaluations already computed during sampling, so no extra network calls are needed. The resulting diagonal covariance Sigma_t is plugged into a PiGDM-style likelihood approximation p(y|xt) ~ N(A x0_hat, sigma^2 I + A Sigma_t A^T), and the guidance gradient Sigma_t A^T (sigma^2 I + A Sigma_t A^T)^{-1} (y - A x0_hat) is computed with conjugate gradients instead of matrix inversion. Experiments cover inpainting (random/box), Gaussian/motion deblurring, and 4x super-resolution on FFHQ and ImageNet, compared against DPS, PiGDM, DDRM, MCG, PnP-ADMM, Score-SDE, and ADMM-TV. No medical imaging (MRI/CT), no Kalman framing, and no measurement selection appear anywhere in the paper.
uses_ensemble_or_policy: No policy network, no offline training, no ensemble. It is single-trajectory and plug-and-play with a pretrained DDPM. Its covariance estimator adds essentially ZERO extra denoiser NFEs per step (it reuses the score from the previous timestep via a temporal finite difference), plus cheap conjugate-gradient iterations involving only the measurement operator A. This is even cheaper per step than our 2-extra-denoiser-call Hutchinson/JVP probe.
overlap_with_ours: COVERED by CA-DPS: (i) the core idea of estimating diag Cov[x0|xt] from a single trajectory of a pretrained diffusion model using Tweedie's second-moment identity, training-free — this is exactly their Theorem 1 + diagonal finite-difference approximation, so we cannot claim novelty for 'single-trajectory Tweedie-based posterior variance estimation' per se; (ii) using that variance to reweight data consistency — their likelihood N(A x0_hat, sigma^2 I + A Sigma_t A^T) reduces, for diagonalizable/subsampled-Fourier A, to precisely the per-frequency Kalman-type gain P_i/(P_i + sigma_noise^2) we propose in component (a), so our variance-gated data-consistency update is anticipated in substance (as it also is by Peng et al.'s 'Optimal Posterior Covariance', OpenReview 9mX0AZVEet). NOT covered: (1) ACTIVE measurement selection — CA-DPS assumes a fixed operator and never selects measurements; our mid-trajectory acquisition of k-space lines / CT angles / pixels scored by projected posterior variance is entirely absent; (2) the specific estimator differs — they use a temporal finite difference of scores across timesteps (which conflates the change in x_t with the change in t and is a heuristic diagonal), whereas we use a Hutchinson probe with a central finite-difference JVP at fixed t (an unbiased diagonal estimator in expectation, at 2 extra NFEs/step) — a technical but defensible distinction we should benchmark against theirs; (3) measurement-domain smoothing (radial k-space smoothing) of the variance map; (4) any medical/multi-domain evaluation (MRI, CT, compressive imaging) or matched-budget acquisition protocol; (5) explicit Kalman filtering interpretation.

title: (1) "Deep probabilistic subsampling for task-adaptive compressed sensing" (DPS); (2) "Active Deep Probabilistic Subsampling" (A-DPS)
authors: DPS: Iris A.M. Huijben, Bastiaan S. Veeling, Ruud J.G. van Sloun. A-DPS: Hans van Gorp, Iris A.M. Huijben, Bastiaan S. Veeling, Nicola Pezzotti, Ruud J.G. van Sloun
venue: DPS: ICLR 2020 (OpenReview). A-DPS: ICML 2021, PMLR vol. 139, pp. 10509-10518
link: https://openreview.net/forum?id=SJeq9JBFvH (DPS) ; https://proceedings.mlr.press/v139/van-gorp21a.html (A-DPS). No arXiv version found for either; code: https://github.com/IamHuijben/Deep-Probabilistic-Subsampling
doi_or_arxiv: None found. DPS: OpenReview ID SJeq9JBFvH; A-DPS: PMLR v139/van-gorp21a (no DOI, no arXiv ID listed in official README/PMLR page)
method_summary: DPS (ICLR 2020) learns WHICH measurements to take jointly with a downstream network: instead of optimizing a binary subsampling matrix A directly, it learns unnormalized logits phi of categorical distributions over the N candidate measurement indices ("generative sampling model P(A|phi)") and draws sample-without-replacement masks via the Gumbel-max trick, backpropagating through a straight-through Gumbel-softmax relaxation so the sampling distribution and the task network (reconstruction or classification) are trained end-to-end. The learned pattern is static: one globally optimized mask applied to all test instances (the A-DPS paper explicitly says DPS "learns a static pattern for all datapoints"). Demonstrated on a toy dataset, MNIST and CIFAR10 in both pixel and spatial-frequency domains. A-DPS (ICML 2021) makes this sequential and instance-adaptive: acquisition proceeds in I=M steps; at each step the task model f_theta produces, besides its prediction, a context vector c_i (e.g. features of the current reconstruction), and a trained sampling network g_kappa (conv layers + LSTM + FC head outputting 208 logits in the MRI case) maps that context to the logits for the next DPS draw. Sampling network and task network are trained jointly offline with a semi-greedy accumulated loss (plus an adversarial discriminator for MRI); the MRI task model is a 3-step unrolled proximal-gradient network. Experiments: MNIST pixel-domain classification and line-based single-coil fastMRI knee reconstruction at 8x acceleration (26 of 208 lines), beating random/low-pass/VDS/greedy/LOUPE/DPS and the active baselines of Zhang et al. 2019 and Pineda et al. 2020.
uses_ensemble_or_policy: Yes — both require offline end-to-end training and A-DPS requires a trained policy. DPS: offline mask optimization; the learned categorical logits ARE trained parameters optimized jointly with a trained task network; the resulting mask is fixed (non-adaptive) at inference. A-DPS: a trained sampling/policy network g_kappa (conv encoder + LSTM + linear head) plus a jointly trained reconstruction/classification network f_theta; both must be retrained per task/operator/sampling budget. Neither uses a diffusion model, posterior sampling, posterior-variance estimation, or an ensemble of posterior samples; inference cost is one task-network forward pass plus one policy forward pass per acquisition step (no NFE-heavy sampling at all — there is no generative sampling trajectory).
overlap_with_ours: Covers: (i) the general idea of optimizing which measurements to acquire under a budget (DPS: offline-learned fixed masks; A-DPS: sequential, instance-adaptive active acquisition conditioned on information acquired so far — conceptually overlapping our "active measurement selection" goal); (ii) some multi-domain framing (pixel-domain and Fourier-domain sampling; MNIST/CIFAR + fastMRI knee k-space lines), though no CT experiments; (iii) matched-budget comparisons against fixed and active baselines in MRI. Does NOT cover: (a) anything training-free — both require full offline joint training and retraining per operator/task/budget, exactly the dependency our method eliminates; (b) diffusion priors or posterior sampling of any kind; (c) single-trajectory Tweedie-second-moment / denoiser-Jacobian posterior-variance estimation (they estimate no uncertainty at all — selection is a learned amortized policy, not an information/variance criterion); (d) variance-gated Kalman-style data consistency (their reconstruction is a trained unrolled network, no per-frequency gain); (e) "mid-trajectory" acquisition interleaved with generative sampling steps — there is no sampling trajectory in their framework. In short: they are the canonical learned-policy active-subsampling baseline our "no policy network, no retraining" claim is defined against, not an anticipation of our mechanism.

title: Adaptive Compressed Sensing with Diffusion-Based Posterior Sampling
authors: Noam Elata, Tomer Michaeli, Michael Elad
venue: ECCV 2024 (Computer Vision – ECCV 2024, 18th European Conference, Milan; Springer LNCS vol. 15136, pp. 290-308)
bibtex:
@inproceedings{elata2024adasense,
  title     = {Adaptive Compressed Sensing with Diffusion-Based Posterior Sampling},
  author    = {Elata, Noam and Michaeli, Tomer and Elad, Michael},
  booktitle = {Computer Vision -- ECCV 2024},
  series    = {Lecture Notes in Computer Science},
  volume    = {15136},
  pages     = {290--308},
  publisher = {Springer},
  year      = {2024},
  doi       = {10.1007/978-3-031-73229-4_17},
  note      = {arXiv:2407.08256}
}
method_summary: AdaSense is a greedy, training-free adaptive compressed-sensing loop built on zero-shot diffusion posterior sampling (DDRM in all experiments). At each of N acquisition rounds it runs the posterior sampler to completion s times conditioned on all measurements acquired so far (y_0:nr), centers the s samples, and selects the next r measurement rows: in the unconstrained case as the top-r right singular vectors (PCA) of the sample matrix, i.e. top eigenvectors of the empirical posterior covariance; in the constrained case (MRI Fourier rows, CT Radon rows) by exhaustively scoring each feasible row H-tilde with the empirical projected posterior variance sum_i x_i^T H-tilde-dagger H-tilde x_i (their Eqs. 5-6). The chosen rows are physically measured, appended to y, and the loop repeats; final reconstruction f(y) is another posterior sample, the mean of several samples, or a domain-specific network (e.g. an MRI reconstructor). Experiments: CelebA-HQ faces (N=8 rounds, r=24, 192 total measurements), FastMRI single-coil knee (vertical R10, general R200/R400, compared against SS-DDQN/DS-DDQN policy baselines from Pineda et al.), and DeepLesion CT sparse-view angle selection. The paper reports it matches training-based active-acquisition policies on MRI without any task-specific training. Stated limitations include dependence on posterior-sampler quality, the high computational cost of generating multiple samples, and restriction to linear measurements.
uses_ensemble_or_policy: No trained policy network and no offline training (fully zero-shot given a pretrained diffusion prior; for MRI/CT they train only the unconditional diffusion prior itself). But it REQUIRES an ensemble of complete posterior samples at inference: s samples per acquisition round, each a full DDRM sampling trajectory, with s kept at ratio 4/3 of r and s >= r required in the constrained (MRI/CT) case. Face experiment: N=8 rounds x s=32 samples = 256 complete posterior-sampling runs per image (NFEs = 256 x DDRM steps; exact step count not stated in the paper, but the authors explicitly list "generating multiple samples requires high computational cost" as a limitation). Measurement selection happens BETWEEN complete sampling runs, never mid-trajectory.
overlap_with_ours: ALREADY COVERED by AdaSense: (1) the high-level concept of training-free, policy-network-free active measurement selection using a pretrained diffusion prior; (2) the selection criterion itself — scoring candidate measurements by projected posterior variance E[(x-E[x|y])^T H^dagger H (x-E[x|y]) | y] is mathematically the same objective as our "score candidate measurements with the projected posterior variance"; (3) multi-domain generality with the same three domains we claim (general CS/pixels, MRI k-space lines, CT projection angles) plus faces; (4) comparison against RL policy baselines showing zero-shot parity. NOT COVERED: (1) our variance estimator — AdaSense uses the empirical covariance of an ensemble of s complete posterior samples, not a single-trajectory Tweedie second-moment / denoiser-Jacobian estimate with a Hutchinson probe (no mention of Tweedie's identity or Jacobians anywhere); (2) mid-trajectory acquisition — AdaSense restarts full posterior sampling between rounds, whereas we select measurements during one sampling trajectory; (3) variance-gated Kalman-style data consistency (per-frequency gain P/(P+sigma^2)) — entirely absent; AdaSense relies on DDRM's hard consistency y=Hx and assumes noiseless measurements; (4) NFE efficiency and matched-NFE evaluation — AdaSense costs hundreds of full trajectories per image (e.g. 256 for faces) vs our 2 extra denoiser calls per step on one trajectory, and it reports no NFE-matched comparisons.

title: Covariance-aware sampling for Diffusion Models
venue: arXiv preprint (stat.ML, cross-listed cs.CV, cs.LG); no journal/conference version found as of 2026-07-07
method_summary: The paper targets few-step UNCONDITIONAL pixel-space diffusion sampling, arguing that few-step samplers degrade because they use only the predicted mean of the reverse transition; it therefore explicitly models the reverse-process covariance Cov[x_{t-1}|x_t]. Using Tweedie's formula, the covariance is obtained analytically as the Jacobian of the denoiser's mean prediction, and is computed cheaply via one extra Jacobian-vector product (autodiff JVP) per sampling step (about 3 function evaluations per step with guidance vs 4 for standard guidance). To make the high-dimensional covariance tractable, they approximate it as (block-)diagonal in a frequency domain — testing Haar/DWT/DCT and a novel ConvDCT transform — with per-frequency-block variances estimated via Hutchinson's trace estimator applied to the JVP outputs. The estimated frequency-wise variances are then used to inject appropriately correlated noise in a DDIM-style update, yielding a plug-in sampler requiring no retraining or architecture changes. Experiments are unconditional/class-conditional generation quality (FID@50k) on ImageNet-512 (SiD2), ImageNet-128 (UViT), and CIFAR-10 at matched NFE, beating Heun, DPM-Solver++, and aDDIM; latent-space Stable Diffusion results were negative due to decoder sensitivity. The paper contains no inverse problems, no data consistency, no measurement models, and no acquisition/active-sensing component of any kind.
uses_ensemble_or_policy: No. It is training-free: no policy network, no offline optimization, no ensemble of posterior samples. It runs a single sampling trajectory with one extra autodiff JVP per step (roughly 1 extra NFE-equivalent per step; ~3 function evaluations per guided step), using a single Hutchinson-style random probe through the denoiser Jacobian.
overlap_with_ours: Substantial overlap on the variance-ESTIMATION machinery, zero overlap on the application. Already covered by this paper: (a) single-trajectory, training-free estimation of diffusion posterior (co)variance via Tweedie's second-moment identity, i.e., covariance = Jacobian of the denoiser mean; (b) computing it with ONE cheap probe per step (their autodiff JVP + Hutchinson block-variance estimator vs our central finite-difference JVP with 2 extra denoiser calls — a minor implementation difference, and theirs estimates Cov[x_{t-1}|x_t] rather than diag Cov[x0|xt], which are related by a known scaling); (c) Fourier/DCT-domain structured (per-frequency, block-diagonal) variance modeling, which closely parallels our radially-smoothed k-space variance map. NOT covered: (1) any linear inverse problem setting — no measurement operator, no DPS/PiGDM guidance, no MRI/CT/inpainting; (2) our variance-gated Kalman-style data-consistency update P_i/(P_i+sigma^2); (3) mid-trajectory ACTIVE measurement selection / adaptive acquisition of any kind; (4) matched-budget acquisition evaluation across measurement domains. So PVAS's core novelty claims (b) and especially (a=Kalman DC, active sensing) survive, but we cannot claim novelty for 'single-probe Tweedie-Jacobian variance estimation with frequency-domain structure' itself — we must present it as adopting/adapting Schioppa & Salimans' estimator to conditional posterior sampling and acquisition.

authors: Tim Bakker, Matthew Muckley, Adriana Romero-Soriano, Michal Drozdzal, Luis Pineda
venue: MIDL 2022 (Proceedings of The 5th International Conference on Medical Imaging with Deep Learning), PMLR vol. 172, pp. 63-85

  author = {Bakker, Tim and Muckley, Matthew and Romero-Soriano, Adriana and Drozdzal, Michal and Pineda, Luis},
  booktitle = {Proceedings of The 5th International Conference on Medical Imaging with Deep Learning},
  pages = {63--85},
  year = {2022},

  series = {Proceedings of Machine Learning Research},

method_summary: Verified from the arXiv abs page, PMLR v172 landing page, and the paper PDF. The paper jointly trains a k-space acquisition policy with an End-to-End Variational Network (E2E VarNet) reconstructor for multi-coil Cartesian 2D MRI (coil-compressed to K=4, 128x128 center-cropped fastMRI knee). Step by step: (1) acquire the ACS (auto-calibration) low-frequency lines; (2) a Policy network - a convolutional feature extractor plus fully-connected block, adapted from Bakker et al. 2020 to complex inputs - takes the ACS k-space/mask (via an ACS-based reconstruction reusing E2E VarNet's sensitivity-map U-Net) and outputs a saliency heatmap, i.e., a sampling probability per candidate k-space column; (3) probabilities are normalized into independent Bernoullis and exactly B additional lines are drawn by rejection sampling in one shot (a single acquisition round conditioned only on the ACS, not step-by-step feedback during scanning); (4) the E2E VarNet, modified with hard data-consistency layers applied sequentially before refinement, reconstructs the image; (5) policy and reconstructor are trained jointly end-to-end for 50 epochs with SSIM loss, backpropagating through the discrete mask via straight-through estimation (sigmoid, slope 10), following Yin et al. 2021. At 4x it performs on par with LOUPE; at 8x it beats the best baseline by ~1.9 SSIM points. Headline finding: the best-performing policies learn to be explicitly NON-adaptive (zero mutual information between input and mask), suggesting adaptivity can over-regularize the reconstruction model.
uses_ensemble_or_policy: Yes - a trained policy network is central: a dedicated CNN+FC Policy network is trained offline, jointly with the E2E VarNet reconstructor, for 50 epochs on fastMRI knee via straight-through gradient estimation (they note Yin et al. 2021 showed this beats RL for this setting). The LOUPE baseline it compares to is offline dataset-level mask optimization. There is NO diffusion model, NO posterior sampling, NO ensemble of posterior samples, and NO uncertainty/variance estimation anywhere in the pipeline. Inference is deterministic and cheap: one Policy-network forward pass to emit the full mask in one shot, then one E2E VarNet forward pass to reconstruct - no iterative NFEs in the diffusion sense.
overlap_with_ours: Overlaps ONLY with the high-level goal of component (b): sample-adaptive selection of k-space lines for undersampled multi-coil MRI under a fixed measurement budget, and it is exactly the 'trained policy network' prior art class PVAS claims to improve upon. It does NOT cover: (i) single-trajectory Tweedie/second-moment posterior-variance estimation (no diffusion prior, no Jacobian/Hutchinson probes, no posterior at all - reconstruction is a deterministic feedforward VarNet); (ii) variance-gated Kalman-style data consistency (it uses hard DC layers with no noise-adaptive gain); (iii) mid-trajectory/sequential active acquisition (its mask is emitted in ONE shot conditioned only on the ACS, before reconstruction - there is no closed-loop acquisition interleaved with inference); (iv) training-free operation (requires joint offline training of policy + reconstructor per dataset/acceleration); (v) multi-domain generality (MRI-only; no CT angles, inpainting, or compressive sensing). Caution for our paper: its central empirical finding - that the best learned policies converge to NON-adaptive masks, i.e., per-sample adaptivity gave no benefit in their multi-coil setup - is a result reviewers will likely raise against any claim that per-sample active selection helps; PVAS should cite this and explain why posterior-variance-driven, mid-trajectory selection with a diffusion prior escapes their negative result (e.g., their adaptivity was one-shot from ACS only, entangled with jointly trained reconstructor regularization).

title: Reducing Uncertainty in Undersampled MRI Reconstruction With Active Acquisition
authors: Zizhao Zhang, Adriana Romero, Matthew J. Muckley, Pascal Vincent, Lin Yang, Michal Drozdzal
venue: CVPR 2019 (Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition), pp. 2049-2058
method_summary: Verified from the arXiv abs page and the paper PDF (Secs. 3-5). The system couples two jointly trained networks: (1) a cascaded FC-ResNet reconstruction network with hard data-consistency layers that maps a zero-filled undersampled MRI to a refined image AND a pixel-wise uncertainty map u(x), trained with a heteroscedastic Gaussian negative log-likelihood (Eq. 2); (2) a discriminator-like "evaluator" network that decomposes the reconstruction into N spectral maps (one per Cartesian k-space row) and is trained (Eqs. 3-4) to score how much each row resembles a truly measured row, with an adversarial term (Eq. 5) pushing the reconstructor to fool it. At inference, active acquisition is an outer greedy loop: the evaluator scores all unobserved rows, the lowest-scored row is acquired next, the input is updated, and the process repeats until a stopping criterion (e.g., low global uncertainty) is met — the uncertainty map itself is used mainly as a halt signal and for error visualization, not as the row-selection score. Everything is trained end-to-end adversarially (K=3 cascades, beta=0.1, gamma=100, 6 Tesla P100 GPUs) on a 10k-volume knee DICOM dataset (k-space simulated by FFT of magnitude images, 128x128) plus grayscale ImageNet. Results: evaluator-guided acquisition beats heuristic active-acquisition baselines, uncertainty correlates with MSE error maps, and the c-ResNet beats pix2pix/U-Net baselines.
uses_ensemble_or_policy: Yes — it requires substantial offline supervised+adversarial training and a trained scoring network. Two task-specific networks must be trained jointly: the reconstruction network (with a learned heteroscedastic variance head) and the evaluator network, which is effectively a greedy one-step policy/critic that ranks candidate k-space rows. No ensemble of posterior samples is used: uncertainty comes from a single forward pass of the learned variance head, and inference costs one reconstruction pass plus one evaluator pass per acquisition step (no diffusion, no NFE notion, no posterior sampling at all). It is NOT training-free and does not transfer across measurement operators without retraining.
overlap_with_ours: Covers: (a) the high-level idea of inference-time active k-space measurement selection guided by a model's assessment of reconstruction quality/uncertainty — this is the canonical CVPR paper for uncertainty-motivated active MRI acquisition, so PVAS's active-selection component is not the first of its kind; (b) producing a per-pixel uncertainty map alongside the reconstruction and showing it correlates with error; (c) greedy sequential acquisition with a stopping criterion. Does NOT cover: (1) no diffusion prior or posterior sampling — reconstruction is a supervised feedforward CNN, so nothing is training-free; (2) no single-trajectory Tweedie-Jacobian posterior variance estimation — uncertainty is a learned aleatoric NLL head, and notably the selection signal is the adversarial evaluator's score, not the posterior variance projected onto candidate measurements (PVAS scores candidates directly with projected posterior variance); (3) no variance-gated Kalman-style data consistency — they use hard DC replacement in k-space; (4) no mid-(sampling)-trajectory acquisition inside a generative trajectory — their loop is an outer loop around a one-shot network; (5) limited generality — Cartesian MRI rows plus an ImageNet toy setting, no CT angles or general linear operators, and both networks must be retrained per domain/operator; (6) uses simulated k-space from DICOM magnitude images, not raw multi-coil data.

title: On the Posterior Distribution in Denoising: Application to Uncertainty Quantification
venue: ICLR 2024 (The Twelfth International Conference on Learning Representations); OpenReview forum adSGeugiuj
method_summary: The paper derives a recursion relating ALL higher-order central moments of the Gaussian-denoising posterior p(x|y) to derivatives of the posterior mean (MMSE denoiser), generalizing Tweedie's formula: in 1D, mu_2(y) = sigma^2 * mu_1'(y) and mu_{k+1}(y) = sigma^2 * mu_k'(y) + k * mu_{k-1}(y) * mu_2(y); in the multivariate case the posterior covariance equals sigma^2 times the denoiser Jacobian. Using this, they compute the top posterior principal components of any pretrained denoiser via power/subspace iteration where each Jacobian-vector product is approximated by a one-sided finite difference of two denoiser forward passes ([mu_1(y+cv) - mu_1(y)]/c), avoiding backprop entirely (they report ~6x memory reduction vs autodiff). They also approximate the full 1D marginal posterior distribution along any direction (e.g., a PC) from the higher-order directional moments via the same finite-difference machinery. The method is entirely training-free and works with any pretrained MMSE denoiser (they test a DDPM denoiser on FFHQ used as a fixed-noise-level Gaussian denoiser, SwinIR on CBSD68/Kodak, MNIST, and Noise2Void on microscopy data). Experiments are uncertainty VISUALIZATION for Gaussian denoising only — no inverse problems, no diffusion posterior-sampling trajectories, no data-consistency mechanism, and no measurement selection.
uses_ensemble_or_policy: No policy network, no offline training, no ensemble of posterior samples — it is training-free and sampling-free, operating on a single noisy image with a pretrained denoiser. Cost: power iteration with finite-difference JVPs, roughly 1 + (iterations x PCs) denoiser forward calls per image/patch (two forward passes per JVP with the base call reusable); no backward passes.
overlap_with_ours: ALREADY COVERS the core estimation primitive we use: (i) the Tweedie second-moment identity Cov[x0|y] = sigma^2 * (denoiser Jacobian) — this is their central theoretical tool (and they go further, to all higher moments); (ii) matrix-free estimation of posterior second-order structure from a pretrained denoiser using finite-difference JVPs (2 forward calls per probe, no autodiff) — essentially the same trick as our central-difference Hutchinson probe, except they use one-sided differences and power iteration for top-k PCs rather than a single Hutchinson probe for the DIAGONAL; (iii) training-free, single-model operation (no ensemble, no policy). DOES NOT COVER: estimating the per-coordinate diagonal variance (they compute principal components/directional marginals, not diag Cov, and no Hutchinson estimator); doing this INSIDE a diffusion posterior-sampling trajectory at every timestep t (they work at a single fixed noise level for pure Gaussian denoising, not with DPS/PiGDM guidance or measurement operators); projecting variance into measurement space (k-space lines, CT angles); (a) any variance-gated Kalman-style data-consistency update; (b) any active/adaptive measurement selection; any inverse-problem or multi-domain (MRI/CT/compressive) application; matched-budget acquisition evaluation. It is pure uncertainty visualization for denoising.

title: Pseudoinverse-Guided Diffusion Models for Inverse Problems
authors: Jiaming Song, Arash Vahdat, Morteza Mardani, Jan Kautz
venue: ICLR 2023 (poster; International Conference on Learning Representations)
doi_or_arxiv: No arXiv version and no DOI exist; the official record is OpenReview forum 9_gsMA8MRKQ (PDF: https://openreview.net/pdf?id=9_gsMA8MRKQ). Verified by search: only OpenReview/ICLR/NVIDIA pages surface, no arxiv.org abs page.
method_summary: PiGDM solves inverse problems y = Hx0 + z (and some non-linear/non-differentiable h) with a pretrained problem-agnostic diffusion model by approximating the intractable guidance score grad_xt log p(y|xt). It approximates the posterior p(x0|xt) as an isotropic Gaussian N(x̂t, r_t^2 I), where x̂t is the one-step MMSE denoised estimate from Tweedie's first-moment formula, and r_t is a fixed analytic scalar schedule r_t^2 = sigma_t^2/(sigma_t^2+1), derived by assuming the data prior is standard normal (Appendix A.3) — it is never estimated from the model or the data. Marginalizing gives p(y|xt) ≈ N(Hx̂t, r_t^2 HH^T + sigma_y^2 I), whose score is (y − Hx̂t)^T (r_t^2 HH^T + sigma_y^2 I)^{-1} H (dx̂t/dxt), computed as a single vector-Jacobian product via backprop through the denoiser; in the noiseless case this reduces to pseudoinverse guidance r_t^{-2}(H†y − H†Hx̂t)^T dx̂t/dxt, generalized to non-linear h via any h† satisfying h(h†(h(x))) = h(x) (e.g., JPEG decode). Each DDIM step adds this guidance term with an implicitly time-adaptive weight (multiplying by r_t^2 in Eq. 10). Sampling is a single trajectory of ~100 steps, each costing one denoiser forward pass plus one backward pass (VJP). Experiments: 4x super-resolution, inpainting (incl. noisy), JPEG restoration, deblurring on ImageNet 256, matching problem-specific diffusion models (SR3, Palette, ADM) and beating DDRM, plus composed measurements (SR+JPEG+masking). The measurement operator is fixed and fully known before sampling begins.
uses_ensemble_or_policy: No policy network, no offline training or mask optimization, and no ensemble of posterior samples. Inference is a single sampling trajectory (they use 100 DDIM steps on ImageNet); per step it costs 1 denoiser forward evaluation plus 1 backprop through the denoiser for the vector-Jacobian product (roughly 2x the cost of unguided DDIM per step, acknowledged as their main limitation vs DDRM). The only diffusion-related training is the standard pretrained unconditional (or class-conditional) score model.
overlap_with_ours: Already covers: (i) training-free guidance with a pretrained problem-agnostic diffusion prior via a Gaussian approximation of p(x0|xt) with Tweedie FIRST-moment mean — this is the backbone we build on; (ii) crucially for our claim (a), its noisy-linear guidance (Eq. 7, Algorithm 1) already applies a Kalman-like gain (r_t^2 HH^T + sigma_y^2 I)^{-1}: for a subsampled-Fourier/diagonalizable H this IS a per-frequency gain of the form P/(P + sigma_noise^2) — except that P = r_t^2 is one global scalar from the analytic heuristic r_t^2 = sigma_t^2/(sigma_t^2+1) (assumes N(0,I) data), identical for every measurement coordinate; (iii) multi-operator generality (SR, inpainting, JPEG, deblurring, composed operators) in the passive setting. Does NOT cover: (1) no estimation of the posterior covariance from the model — it never uses Tweedie's second-moment identity Cov[x0|xt] = sigma_t^2 * denoiser Jacobian; the Jacobian appears only inside the guidance VJP, never as a variance estimate, and there is no Hutchinson/probing diagonal estimator; (2) therefore no per-coordinate, data-adaptive variance map and no variance smoothing — our variance-gated update replaces their global scalar r_t^2 with estimated diag Cov, which is exactly the delta we must state; (3) no active or adaptive measurement selection of any kind — H is fixed before sampling; no mid-trajectory acquisition, no candidate scoring, no MRI/CT experiments (MRI is only mentioned as future potential); (4) no uncertainty quantification output at all.

title: Tweedie Moment Projected Diffusions For Inverse Problems
authors: Benjamin Boys, Mark Girolami, Jakiw Pidstrigach, Sebastian Reich, Alan Mosca, O. Deniz Akyildiz
venue: Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR), published 09/2024; arXiv:2310.06721 (stat.CO), v1 Oct 2023, v3 Sep 25 2024
method_summary: TMPD solves linear inverse problems y = Hx0 + noise with a pretrained unconditional diffusion prior by building a Gaussian approximation to p(x0|xt) using BOTH Tweedie moments: the mean m0|t from Tweedie's first-order formula, and the covariance C0|t = (v_t/sqrt(alpha_t)) * Jacobian_{xt} m0|t from Tweedie's second-moment identity (verified in their Prop. 1 and Eq. 9 of the arXiv HTML). At each reverse step the guidance term is a Kalman-gain-style projected update, Eq. (11): grad term = (Jacobian of m0|t) H^T (H C0|t H^T + sigma_y^2 I)^{-1} (y - H m0|t), i.e., data consistency is gated per-measurement by the projected posterior covariance plus noise variance — exactly a per-coordinate gain P/(P+sigma^2) structure when H C H^T is (approximately) diagonal. Practically they offer: full TMPD (Jacobian via vector-Jacobian products / solves), DTMPD (diagonal-of-Jacobian approximation), and for images a row-sum-of-the-Jacobian diagonal approximation computable with a single VJP, exploiting mask sparsity, at about 1.5x the runtime of PiGDM/DPS. They prove a theoretical guarantee for posterior sampling, remove time-dependent step-size hyperparameters of DPS/PiGDM, and show stability with variance-exploding processes. Experiments: Gaussian mixture posteriors (80-800 dim, exact Wasserstein comparison), Gaussian random fields, and image inpainting/super-resolution with pretrained diffusion models (PSNR/LPIPS). No MRI, no CT, and no measurement-selection component anywhere in the paper.
uses_ensemble_or_policy: No policy network, no offline training, no ensemble. It runs a SINGLE posterior-sampling trajectory. Per step: one score-network forward evaluation plus vector-Jacobian products through the denoiser via autodiff (the image-scale row-sum variant needs a single VJP per step, reported ~1.5x the wall-clock of PiGDM/DPS; the full variant needs more JVP/VJP work for the (H C H^T + sigma^2 I)^{-1} solve).
overlap_with_ours: ALREADY COVERED by TMPD: (i) using Tweedie's second-moment identity Cov[x0|xt] = sigma_t^2 * denoiser Jacobian to get per-coordinate posterior variance from a single trajectory (no ensemble); (ii) our part (a) almost exactly — the variance-gated Kalman-style data-consistency update with per-measurement gain involving (H C0|t H^T + sigma_noise^2 I)^{-1}, i.e., P_i/(P_i + sigma^2) when diagonal — this is TMPD's Eq. (11) and the paper's central contribution, including diagonal approximations of the Jacobian for image-scale problems; (iii) theoretical grounding for this Gaussian-projection guidance. NOT COVERED by TMPD: (1) our specific estimator — a single Hutchinson probe with central finite-difference JVP (2 extra denoiser forward calls, no autodiff/backprop through the network) plus domain-aware smoothing (radial k-space averaging); TMPD uses autodiff VJPs and row-sum/diagonal analytic approximations instead; (2) our part (b) entirely — mid-trajectory ACTIVE measurement selection / adaptive acquisition scored by projected posterior variance (TMPD assumes a fixed, given H); (3) MRI k-space, CT angle, or compressive-sensing acquisition applications and matched-budget/matched-NFE active-sensing evaluation; (4) any cross-operator active-sensing generality claims.

title: Free Hunch: Denoiser Covariance Estimation for Diffusion Models Without Extra Costs
authors: Severi Rissanen, Markus Heinonen, Arno Solin (Aalto University)
venue: ICLR 2025 (Thirteenth International Conference on Learning Representations); PDF header reads "Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025"; OpenReview forum 4JK2XMGUc8
method_summary: Free Hunch (FH) estimates the denoiser posterior covariance Cov[x0|xt] for diffusion models to improve training-free guidance in linear inverse problems, verified from the full paper text (arXiv:2410.11149v2). (1) It initializes Sigma_{0|t} at t=T with the training-data covariance, approximated as diagonal in the DCT basis for images. (2) A "time update" transfers the covariance across noise levels in closed form via a local Gaussian approximation of p(xt) under the forward SDE: Sigma_{0|t+dt}^{-1} = Sigma_{0|t}^{-1} + (sigma(t+dt)^{-2} - sigma(t)^{-2}) I. (3) A "space update" adds curvature information using the denoiser evaluations that already occur during sampling: since Cov[x0|xt] = sigma_t^2 * Jacobian of E[x0|xt] (second-order Tweedie), consecutive denoiser means along the trajectory give a secant condition sigma_t^2 (mu(x+dx) - mu(x)) ~ Sigma dx, which drives BFGS-style rank-2 updates; the covariance is stored as diagonal + low-rank (D + UU^T - VV^T) with Woodbury inversions. (4) The covariance is plugged into PiGDM/reconstruction-style guidance for linear-Gaussian observations, grad log p(y|xt) = (y - A mu)^T (A Sigma A^T + sigma_y^2 I)^{-1} A grad mu, solved with conjugate gradient. They also prove that identity/zero covariances (DPS, PiGDM) systematically overestimate guidance scale for correlated data. Experiments: synthetic Gaussian mixtures and ImageNet 256x256 (Gaussian deblur, motion deblur, random inpainting, 4x super-resolution) at 15/30 Heun steps, beating DPS, PiGDM, TMPD, and Peng et al. baselines especially at low step counts.
uses_ensemble_or_policy: No policy network, no offline training, no mask optimization, and no ensemble of posterior samples. It runs on a SINGLE sampling trajectory and — its headline claim — requires ZERO extra network function evaluations: the BFGS space updates reuse the denoiser calls the sampler already makes (15/30 Heun steps in experiments), and time updates plus DCT-diagonal + low-rank algebra are cheap linear-algebra operations. This is strictly cheaper than PVAS's proposed 2 extra denoiser calls per step for the Hutchinson finite-difference probe.
overlap_with_ours: ALREADY COVERED by FH: (i) single-trajectory, training-free estimation of Cov[x0|xt] via the second-order Tweedie identity (covariance = sigma_t^2 * denoiser Jacobian) — FH's BFGS secant condition is precisely a finite-difference directional derivative (JVP) of the denoiser mean, using the trajectory's own steps as probe directions instead of our random Hutchinson probes, and it costs 0 extra NFEs versus our +2 per step; (ii) frequency-domain structured variance — FH's base covariance is diagonal in the DCT basis, closely analogous to our radially-smoothed k-space diagonal for MRI; (iii) variance-weighted data consistency — FH's guidance (A Sigma A^T + sigma_y^2 I)^{-1} residual weighting is mathematically the same per-frequency Kalman-gain structure P_i/(P_i + sigma_noise^2) as our variance-gated update when A is subsampled Fourier and Sigma is frequency-diagonal, so component (a) of PVAS is substantially anticipated. NOT COVERED: (iv) active/adaptive measurement selection — FH assumes a FIXED measurement operator and never chooses which measurements to acquire; there is no mid-trajectory acquisition, no candidate-measurement scoring, no matched-budget acquisition protocol; (v) no MRI k-space, CT-angle, or compressive-sensing acquisition experiments (only deblurring/inpainting/super-resolution on ImageNet); (vi) no analysis of using the projected posterior variance as an acquisition utility. So PVAS component (b) — posterior-variance-guided active sensing — remains open relative to this paper, but component (a) needs to be repositioned as an application of (or improvement over) FH-style covariance estimation rather than a novel contribution.
